senses.definition: Occurring quickly with little or no warning or expectation; instantly.
examples: The sudden drop in temperature left everyone cold and confused.

quotes.text: From lightninges and tempeſtes, from plage, peſtilence, and famine, from battayle and murther, and from ſodayn death. / Good lord deliver us.
quotes.reference: 1552, The Boke of Common Prayer [etc.], The Letanie:

quotes.text: I stumbled along through the young pines and huckleberry bushes. Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path that, I cal'lated, might lead to the road I was hunting for. It twisted and turned, and, the first thing I knew, made a sudden bend around a bunch of bayberry scrub and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn.

senses.definition: (obsolete) Hastily prepared or employed; quick; rapid.

quotes.text: Never was such a sudden scholar made.
quotes.reference: c. 1599, William Shakespeare, Henry V, act 1, scene 1:

quotes.text: Thus these pious flourishes and colours, examined thoroughly, are like the apples of Asphaltis, appearing goodly to the sudden eye; but look well upon them, or at least but touch them, and they turn into cinders.

And if along with these should come
⁠The man I held as half-divine;
⁠Should strike a sudden hand in mine,
And ask a thousand things of home; […]
I should not feel it to be strange.

quotes.text: I have no joy of this contract to-night: / It is too rash, too unadvised, too sudden;
quotes.reference: c. 1591–1595, William Shakespeare, Romeo and Juliet, act 2, scene 2:

quotes.text: Herbs of every leaf that sudden flowered.
